name: Rushes and sedges
note: Rushes and sedges (docs 10, 14): the marsh's own sward, a cover plant like grass, so a share per square meter rather than plants one by one. habitat: each axis [ideal low, ideal high, tolerance] as in reeds.json; rushes want still, shallow fresh water or soaked ground (a marsh, a pond's shallow edge, a damp hollow), never running water or salt. growth: the cover per square meter moves ratePerH of the gap toward how well rushes like the ground each game hour, so a drained marsh thins out; a new island starts with it full where the ground suits it (they were here when you arrived). spread: rushes only take bare ground next to a stand (a neighbouring square at least fromShare full), so they creep out about a meter a day; and in any hour, with chance jumpPerH, a seed carried off a stand lands within jumpM meters (jumpTries landings are tried, most on ground that will not do) and starts a tussock (jumpStart of full) where the ground suits it at least jumpMinSuit, so a new marsh far from any rushes waits to be found. plantStart: how full the square a player plants (the Plant tool) starts. Drawn as stiff upright blades by grass-blades.wgsl, which stand on the bed and rise out of water up to maxWaterM deep. blades: as grass.json (height, width, variation, rest lean, root shade); stems lean out from their tussock's core, so a tussock splays; pixelWidth keeps far stems at least that many pixels wide, so thin stems never break into dots on a phone. clumps: rushes grow in tussocks clumpM across with open water between them; threshold is how much of the cover's ground the tussocks fill at full cover (0.5 about half, higher less), sparse raises it where the cover is thin, edge softens a tussock's rim, and core is how much taller the middle of a tussock stands than its rim. density, wind and season as grass.json; on a tier with thinner grass (quality-tiers grassDensity under 1) stems widen tierWiden of the way toward covering the same ground, so tussocks keep their mass on a phone; season albedo is physical (linear), tips brown in autumn and winter.
